quizName: DMV Practice Test #16 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: When being passed from behind, what should you do?

options.text: Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: The center portion of the lane is safest when being passed. Riding on the side nearest the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding on the far side may make the other driver return to your lane too soon.

questions.question: For a long trip, what should you do?

options.text: Take as few rest breaks as possible.
Use caffeine or other stimulants if you feel sleepy.
Dress warmly to protect against cold weather.
Ride more than 12 hours per day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dress warmly to protect against cold weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Ride no more than six hours per day and take breaks every two hours. Do not use stimulants because extreme fatigue follows when they wear off.

questions.question: If your front wheel skids from braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release both brakes and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and apply it again smoothly.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks from braking, release it immediately and then apply it again smoothly.

questions.question: When riding in a group, what should you do?

options.text: Put inexperienced riders at the back.
Do not follow too closely behind other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not follow too closely behind other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation. Check mirrors often. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep proper space between all riders in the group.

questions.question: Fatigue can increase when you:

options.text: Start riding late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in cool weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from wind, rain, and cold. Ride no more than six hours per day and take breaks every two hours. Avoid stimulants because fatigue gets worse when they wear off.

questions.question: When preparing to pass another vehicle on the left, which part of the lane should you use?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left portion
questions.explanation: Ride in the left portion of the lane when passing to see better and be more visible to oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When choosing a lane position, what should you do?

options.text: Always ride in the center of the lane.
Always ride in the left portion of the lane.
Always ride in the right portion of the lane.
Change position based on different conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change position based on different conditions.
questions.explanation: There is no single best lane position. Choose the portion where you are most visible and can keep space around you.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down suddenly.
When a stop sign is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before slowing suddenly. A tailgater may not see hazards ahead that you are avoiding.

questions.question: Your riding clothes should protect you from all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: Chapped lips.
questions.explanation: Your clothes should protect you from sunburn, windburn, rain, dehydration, cold, and motorcycle parts. They should also protect you if you crash.

questions.question: When entering a turn, a rider should:

options.text: Lean their shoulders to match the turn angle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Before entering a turn, slow down by releasing the throttle and applying both brakes if needed.

questions.question: When is it most important to flash your brake light?

options.text: When you need to slow down suddenly.
When there is a stop sign ahead.
When your signals do not work.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you need to slow down suddenly.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is not as noticeable as a car's or truck's brake lights. Flashing your brake light helps other drivers see that you are slowing down, especially when you slow down faster than they expect.

questions.question: If you lock the rear tire on a dry road surface, what should you do?

options.text: Release and re-apply the rear brake.
Keep it locked until you completely stop.
Release the rear brake and only use the front brake.
Release the rear brake and use both brakes to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until you completely stop.
questions.explanation: If you lock the rear brake on a dry road, you can keep it locked until you stop completely. You can still steer your motorcycle with a locked rear wheel.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Right turn
questions.explanation: You can use hand signals instead of or along with turn signals to show your intentions. When your left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means you plan to turn right or move right.

questions.question: Most motorcycles have curved, or convex, mirrors. What do these mirrors do?

options.text: Are easy to get used to right away.
Make cars seem closer than they actually are.
Show a narrow view of the road.
Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make cars seem farther away than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you than flat mirrors do. They also make objects appear farther away than they really are. Practice judging distances in convex mirrors if you are not used to them.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Encourage other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you out of blind spots and away from wind blasts and hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide an escape route if needed.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following except:

options.text: Allow you to set up for turns.
Help you avoid wind blasts from other vehicles.
Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place you in another vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: A good lane position should help you see others and be seen. It should keep you out of blind spots and away from wind blasts and hazards. Your lane position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and provide an escape route if needed.

questions.question: If you must both brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do one action, then the other.
Do both at the same time and brake harder.
Do both at the same time, but focus mainly on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: You need good grip on the road to swerve safely, so you should not brake and swerve at the same time. If you must both brake and swerve, do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: A passenger must wear a helmet if:

options.text: They are under 25 years of age.
There is a lot of traffic on the road.
The operator is required by law to wear a helmet.
They do not have a motorcycle license.

questions.correctAnswerText: The operator is required by law to wear a helmet.
questions.explanation: Any motorcycle operator or passenger under age 18 must wear a helmet that meets U.S. standards. If the operator must wear a helmet by law, then passengers must also wear one, regardless of age. It is recommended that all riders wear helmets on every ride.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you NOT do?
questions.correctAnswerText: Brake quickly.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, you should slow down, avoid sudden movements, and use both brakes gently if you need to brake.

questions.question: What is the minimum following distance you should maintain?
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds
questions.explanation: You should keep at least two seconds of distance behind the vehicle ahead of you. Increase this to at least three seconds when riding conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: A rectangular sign shows a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular. They are white with black lettering. These signs tell drivers the rules of the road. You must follow them.

questions.question: If another driver is following too closely, you should:

options.text: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn the other driver.
Pull over to the side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flash your brake light before slowing down to warn the other driver.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light before you slow down. This warns the driver behind you. They may not see hazards ahead that require slowing down.

questions.question: When crossing railroad tracks next to the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Cross at a 45-degree angle.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks at a 45-degree angle or more. Move to a lane that lets you do this. Then turn sharply and quickly. If you inch across slowly, your tires can get caught and throw you off balance.

questions.question: Which sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: You may not need extra space between cars if:

options.text: You cannot see past the vehicle ahead.
The weather and traffic are perfect.

questions.correctAnswerText: The weather and traffic are perfect.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space between cars in bad conditions. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, you cannot see ahead, or traffic is heavy.
